title: Course Page Template: User Guide
text:
Welcome to the SciLifeLab Course Webpage Template User Guide!
The SciLifeLab Course Webpage Template is designed to help course organisers create consistent, reusable, and FAIR training materials with minimal technical knowledge.
This guide explains how to set up, customise, publish, and maintain a course website using the template. Whether you are creating a new course or updating an existing one, the guide provides step-by-step instructions for each stage of the process.
By the end of this guide, you will know how to:

Create a new course repository from the template.
Set up the repository on your computer and preview the website locally.
Customise the course landing page.
Create and manage course instances.
Customise course instance pages.
Publish updates to your course website using GitHub.
Prepare your training materials for publication, citation, and reuse following FAIR principles.

The guide assumes no prior experience with Git, GitHub, or Quarto. Each chapter explains where to find the relevant files, what to edit, and how to preview your changes before publishing them.



This User Guide is maintained by SciLifeLab Training Hub.
If you have questions, encounter problems, or have suggestions for improving the guide or the SciLifeLab Course Webpage Template, please open an issue in the SciLifeLab Course Webpage Template GitHub repository or contact SciLifeLab Training Hub at training@scilifelab.se.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
2.1 Create accounts
This chapter explains how to create your own copy of the SciLifeLab Course Page Template, set it up on your computer, and publish your first changes. By the end of it, you will have your own course repository, be able to edit and preview the course website locally, and know how to publish updates to GitHub.
You do not need prior experience with Git, GitHub, Visual Studio Code, or Quarto. Each section provides step-by-step instructions to help you get your course website up and running.
In the following sections, you will learn how to:
Each section explains what to do, where to do it, and what you should expect to see before moving on to the next step.
At the end of each section, you will also find a Quick reference box summarising the key steps. These boxes provide a quick reminder of the files, tools, or actions involved and are useful when you return to the guide after completing the initial setup.
Before creating your course repository, make sure you have access to the software and accounts needed to work with the SciLifeLab Course Page Template.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
2.1.1 1. Create a GitHub account
GitHub is used to store your course repository, collaborate with others, and publish your course website.
If you do not already have a GitHub account:

Visit https://github.com.
Click Sign up.
Follow the instructions to create an account.

If your course repository will be hosted within a GitHub organisation (for example SciLifeLab-Training, SciLifeLabDataCentre, or NBISweden), ask an organisation administrator to add your GitHub account as a member before continuing.
Screenshot: GitHub sign-up page.


2.1.2 2. Install Visual Studio Code
Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is the editor used throughout this guide to edit and preview the course website.
If you do not already have VS Code installed:

Visit https://code.visualstudio.com/.
Download the version for your operating system.
Follow the installation instructions.

After installation, open VS Code once to check that it starts correctly.
Screenshot: Visual Studio Code download page.






Tip



Throughout this guide, all file editing and Git operations are demonstrated using Visual Studio Code. You may use a different editor if you prefer, but the instructions and screenshots assume you are using VS Code.

title: 2  Getting started
section: 2.2 Create a repository from the template
text:
2.2 Create a repository from the template
The first step is to create your own copy of the SciLifeLab Course Webpage Template. This creates a new repository for your course, while leaving the original template unchanged.

2.2.1 Open the template repository
In your web browser, open the SciLifeLab Course Webpage Template.
In the top-right corner of the page, click the green Use this template button and select Create a new repository.
image: fig-alt=“GitHub repository page showing the Use this template button.”


2.2.2 Configure your new repository
GitHub will open the Create a new repository page.

At the top of the page, make sure Include all branches is turned on.
Under Owner, select the GitHub organisation or account where the course repository should be hosted (e.g. SciLifeLabDataCentre, SciLifeLab-Training, NBISweden, Stockholm University, or your personal GitHub account).







Note



If the organisation you need does not appear under Owner, contact an administrator or owner of that organisation to request access.



Under Repository name, enter a name for your course repository. Use lowercase letters where possible and separate words with hyphens (-), for example introduction-to-r.







Tip



Choose the repository name carefully. The repository name becomes part of the URL of your published course website.



Optionally, add a short description of your course.
Choose the repository visibility. For most courses, select Public so that the course website and training materials can be accessed by others. Select Private only if access to the repository and course materials should be restricted.
Click Create repository.

image: fig-alt=“GitHub form for creating a repository from a template, including the owner, repository name, visibility and Include all branches options.


2.2.3 Check your new repository
GitHub will create the repository and automatically open its main page.
Check the repository name at the top of the page to make sure you are now working in your new course repository, rather than the original SciLifeLab Course Page Template repository.
 image: fig-alt=“GitHub page showing a newly created repository based on the course page template.”


2.2.4 Add collaborators
If other people will help develop or maintain the course, you can give them access to the repository. If you do not yet know who will contribute, you can return to this step later.

In your course repository, click Settings.
Under Access in the menu on the left, click Collaborators and teams.

fig-alt=“GitHub repository settings with Collaborators and teams selected under Access.”

Click Add people or Add teams, depending on who you want to give access to.


Search for the GitHub user or team.
Select the appropriate repository role.
Click Add to confirm.







Note



The options available under Collaborators and teams depend on whether the repository belongs to a personal GitHub account or a GitHub organisation, and on your permissions within that organisation.


Your course repository is now ready to use. In the next section, you will create a local copy of the repository on your computer so that you can begin editing the course website.

title: 2  Getting started
section: 2.3 Clone the repository to your computer
text:
2.3 Clone the repository to your computer
You now have your course repository on GitHub. The next step is to create a copy of it on your computer so that you can edit, preview, and test the course website locally.
Creating a copy of a GitHub repository on your computer is called cloning.
Any changes you make remain on your computer until you commit and push them back to GitHub. This gives you the opportunity to preview your changes, experiment safely, and fix any mistakes before they become visible to collaborators or visitors to your course website.

2.3.1 Copy the repository URL
On the main page of your course repository, click the green Code button.
Make sure HTTPS is selected, then copy the repository URL.
Screenshot: GitHub Code menu showing the HTTPS repository URL.


2.3.2 Clone the repository
First, decide where you would like to keep your GitHub repositories on your computer. A common choice is to create a folder called GitHub inside your Documents folder.
You will then use a terminal to navigate to this location and clone the repository.

To navigate to your chosen folder, open a terminal and use the command cd

For example, to use a GitHub folder inside Documents on macOS, copy and paste the following into the terminal:
cd ~/Documents/GitHub
Screenshot: Terminal showing the command above.






Tip



You only need to choose this location once. When you clone the repository, Git will automatically create a new folder with the repository name inside this location.



To then clone your new repository into this folder, copy and paste the following into your terminal:

git clone REPOSITORY-URL
Replace REPOSITORY-URL with the HTTPS URL you copied from GitHub.
For example:
git clone https://github.com/ORGANISATION/my-course.git
Screenshot: Terminal showing the completed git clone command.
Git will download the repository and create a new folder containing all of the files needed for your course website.
You now have a local copy of your course repository. In the next section, you will open it in Visual Studio Code and prepare it for editing.

Quick reference
 Clone the repository to your computer

section: 2.4 Open the repository in Visual Studio Code

2.4 Open the repository in Visual Studio Code
Throughout this guide, you will use Visual Studio Code (VS Code) to edit your course website, preview your changes, and manage the repository.
To open your new repository in VS Code:

Open Visual Studio Code.
From the menu bar, select: File → Open Folder…
Navigate to the repository you just cloned, select the repository folder, and click Open.

Screenshot: VS Code showing the Open Folder dialog with the cloned repository selected.
The files and folders in your repository should now appear in the Explorer panel on the left-hand side of the window.
Throughout this guide, you will edit files by selecting them from the Explorer.
Screenshot: VS Code showing the Explorer panel with the repository opened.
You are now ready to set up the local environment needed to edit and preview your course website.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
2.5 Set up the local environment
Before you can preview and edit your course website in VS Code, you need to prepare the local environment on your computer. For this, you can simply copy and paste the commands below into the terminal exactly as shown.

2.5.1 Open a terminal
To open a terminal in VS Code, select Terminal → New Terminal.
A terminal should open at the bottom of the VS Code window.
Screenshot: VS Code showing Terminal → New Terminal.


2.5.2 Create a virtual environment
Copy and paste the following command into the terminal, then press Enter.
python3 -m venv .venv


2.5.3 Activate the virtual environment
Next, copy and paste the following command into the terminal, and press Enter:
source .venv/bin/activate
If the command was successful, you should see (.venv) at the beginning of the terminal prompt.
For example:
(.venv) username@computer my-course %
Screenshot: Terminal showing (.venv) at the beginning of the prompt.


2.5.4 3. Install the required software
Finally, copy and paste the following commands into the terminal, and press Enter:
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
This may take a minute or two. Once the installation is complete, your local environment is ready and you can preview your course website.






Tip



You only need to create the virtual environment and install the required software once for each course repository.
The next time you work on the repository, simply open a terminal in VS Code and reactivate the virtual environment by running:
source .venv/bin/activate
You should again see (.venv) at the beginning of the terminal prompt.



Quick reference
 Set up the local environment

title: 2  Getting started
text:
2.6 Preview the course website
You are now ready to preview your course website on your computer.
The SciLifeLab Course Page Template uses Quarto to build the website. Before publishing any changes, you can preview the website locally in your web browser to check that everything looks as expected.
The preview is only visible on your own computer. This allows you to safely experiment, edit, and test your course website before your changes become visible to collaborators or visitors.

2.6.1 Start the preview - terminal
To start the preview, open a terminal in VS Code. In the terminal, run:
quarto preview
Quarto will build the website and, after a few seconds, display an address similar to:
http://localhost:4268/
In most cases, this page will open automatically in your default web browser. If it does not, copy the address from the terminal and open it manually in your browser.
fig-alt=“Course landing page displayed locally in a web browser using Quarto preview.”


2.6.2 Start the preview - preview button
Alternatively, you can start the preview directly from VS Code by clicking the Open Preview button in the top-right corner of the editor.
Screenshot: VS Code showing the Open Preview button.
This opens the website inside VS Code. To view the website in your default web browser, click the Open in Browser button.
Screenshot: VS Code preview with the Open in Browser button highlighted.


2.6.3 Preview your changes
The website you are viewing is a local preview. It is only available on your computer and is not visible to anyone else.
As you edit and save files in VS Code, Quarto automatically rebuilds the website and refreshes the preview in your browser. This allows you to see your changes automatically without restarting the preview.


2.6.4 Stop the preview
While the preview is running, the terminal is being used by Quarto. If you need to run other commands without stopping the preview, open a second terminal in VS Code.
When you are finished, return to the terminal where quarto preview is running and press Ctrl+C to stop the preview.






Tip



You can start the preview at any time by either:

running

quarto preview

clicking the Open Preview button in VS Code.

Whenever you return to work on your course, remember to first activate the virtual environment by running:
source .venv/bin/activate



Quick reference
 Preview the course website

Click the Open Preview button.


View the website in your browser

Save the file. The preview refreshes automatically.

title: 2  Getting started
text:
2.7 Commit and push your changes
So far, any changes you will make exist only on your own computer.
To make changes available to collaborators and publish them on your course website, you need to commit and push them to GitHub.
In this section, you will make a small change to the landing page and publish it to your repository.

2.7.1 1. Make a small change
Open _sections/hero.qmd.
Change the course title to something recognisable, for example:
My first course website
Save the file.
If quarto preview is running, the preview should refresh automatically and display the updated title.
Screenshot: Updated course title in the preview.


2.7.2 2. Open Source Control
In Visual Studio Code, click the Source Control icon in the Activity Bar on the left-hand side.
You should now see the files that have changed since you cloned the repository.
Screenshot: Source Control showing modified files.


2.7.3 3. Stage the changes
Click the + button next to Changes to stage all modified files.
Staging tells Git which changes you want to include in the next commit.
Screenshot: Stage Changes button.


2.7.4 4. Commit the changes
At the top of the Source Control panel, enter a short description of your changes.
For example:
Update course title
Click Commit.
Screenshot: Commit message box and Commit button.


2.7.5 5. Push the changes to GitHub
After committing, click Sync Changes.
Visual Studio Code will push your changes to GitHub.
Screenshot: Sync Changes button.
Once the push is complete, your changes have been uploaded to your GitHub repository.

2.8 View the published website
When you push to main, GitHub automatically rebuilds and republishes the landing page. Then show Actions tab green checkmark Pages

2.9 Next steps
Congratulations! You now have your own copy of the SciLifeLab Course Page Template running locally and published through GitHub Pages. Continue with: Landing page to customise the landing page. Course instances to create and manage course instances. FAIRification to prepare your training materials for publication and reuse.

title: 3  Repository structure
text:
3.1 Branches
By default, GitHub displays the main branch. This branch contains the course landing page and general information about your course.
The template also contains additional branches used for course instances and publication. You will work with these later in the guide.

title: 3  Repository structure
text:
Note



The course website uses different branches for different purposes:

main contains the course landing page and general course information.
Course instance branches contain the training materials for individual course runs.
gh-pages contains the published website and is managed automatically.

You should not edit the gh-pages branch directly.

title: 4  Landing page
text:
4.1 Remove the template banner
The landing page introduces your course and provides visitors with the information they need to decide whether they want to register for your course or access a course instance.
The figure below shows the main sections of the landing page and the terminology used throughout this guide.
In the following sections, you will find how to:
Each section in this chapter explains which file to edit and provides step-by-step instructions.
At the end of each section, you will also find a Quick reference box summarising the most important changes. These boxes show you at a glance which file to edit and what to change, and can be useful when you return to the guide after you are already familiar with the individual steps.
The yellow banner at the top of the landing page provides a link to this User Guide. It is included to help you set up and customise the template and is not intended to remain on your course website.
Once you are ready to use the template for your own course, you can remove the banner.

text:

If you do want to delete the file:

title: 4  Landing page
section: 4.2 Hero: Change the course title and subtitle
text:
4.2 Hero: Change the course title and subtitle
The hero is the large banner at the top of the landing page. It is the first thing visitors see when they open your course website and contains the course title, subtitle, logos, and ‘current course instance’ and ‘registration’ action buttons.

4.2.1 Change the course title

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the following lines:

:::{.hero__title}
Course title
:::

Replace Course title with the title of your course.



4.2.2 Change the course subtitle

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the following lines:

:::{.hero__subtitle}
Course subtitle
:::

Replace Course subtitle with a one-line description of your course.







Tip



Keep the subtitle to one sentence and start with an action verb such as Learn, Understand, Explore, Build, or Apply.
For example:

Learn how to apply open science practices throughout the research lifecycle.




 Quick reference 
 Change course title and subtitle 








To…
File
Edit




Change the course title
_sections/hero.qmd
Replace the text between :::{.hero__title} and :::.


Change the course subtitle
_sections/hero.qmd
Replace the text between :::{.hero__subtitle} and :::.

title: 4  Landing page
section: 4.3 Hero: Add or remove a logo
text:
4.3 Hero: Add or remove a logo
The logos displayed in the hero banner represent the organisations associated with your course. You can add additional logos, remove existing ones, or replace them with your own.

4.3.1 Add a logo

Save your logo as a PNG or SVG file.







Tip



If possible, use a white version of your logo so that it contrasts well with the dark background of the hero banner.



In the main branch, open the img folder, then the logos folder.
Copy your logo file into the folder.

VS Code: Drag and drop the file into the folder.
GitHub Desktop: Click Add file, then Upload files.

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the following block:

<div class="hero__brand-item">
  <img src="img/logos/SciLifeLab_Logotype_NEG.png"
       alt="SciLifeLab"
       class="hero__partner-logo">
</div>

Copy the entire block and paste it directly below the existing one.
Replace only the src and alt values with those for your own logo.

For example:
<div class="hero__brand-item">
  <img src="img/logos/your-logo-file.png"
       alt="Your organisation"
       class="hero__partner-logo">
</div>


4.3.2 Remove a logo

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the logo block you want to remove.

For example:
<div class="hero__brand-item">
  <img src="img/logos/SciLifeLab_Logotype_NEG.png"
       alt="SciLifeLab"
       class="hero__partner-logo">
</div>

Delete the entire <div class="hero__brand-item">...</div> block.
OPTIONAL: If you no longer need the logo image, you can also delete it from the img/logos folder.

VS Code: Right-click the file and select Delete.
GitHub Desktop: Open the repository, locate the file, click the three dots (⋮), and choose Delete file.



 Quick reference 
 Add or remove a logo 








To…
File
Edit




Add a logo
img/logos
Copy your logo image (.png or .svg) into the folder.


Display a logo on the landing page
_sections/hero.qmd
Copy an existing <div class="hero__brand-item">...</div> block and update the src and alt attributes.


Remove a logo from the landing page
_sections/hero.qmd
Delete the corresponding <div class="hero__brand-item">...</div> block.


Delete an unused logo file (optional)
img/logos
Delete the logo image if it is no longer needed.

title: 4  Landing page
section: 4.4 Hero: Configure the current course instance and registration action buttons
text:
4.4 Hero: Configure the current course instance and registration action buttons
The hero can display two action buttons:

Take me to the current course instance links visitors to the current published course instance.
Register now links visitors to the course registration page.

You can change these buttons’ links and text, or hide them when they are not needed.

4.4.1 Add a link to the current course instance button

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Locate the course instance with:

status: current

Update slug, label, instance_url, and sort_key to match the current course instance.







Important



The values of slug and instance_url must match!


For example:
instances:
  - slug: "0000"
    label: "May 2026"
    status: current
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: true
    instance_url: "./0000/"
    registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
    sort_key: 200000
For a course instance taught in May 2026, this could become:
instances:
  - slug: "2605"
    label: "May 2026"
    status: current
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: true
    instance_url: "./2605/"
    registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
    sort_key: 202605






Tip



In this template, each course instance is generated from a repository branch and is named using the year and month in which the instance is taught.
For example, a course taught in May 2026 uses 2605. Its relative course instance URL is therefore ./2605/.




4.4.2 Add a link to the registration button
If registration for your training is open, you can display the Register now button and link it directly to your registration page.

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Locate the course instance with:

status: current

Find registration_url:

registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"

Replace the example URL with the URL of your course registration page.

For example:
registration_url: "https://your-registration-page.example"


4.4.3 Hide the current course instance button
If you don’t have a current course instance (e.g. if the course is self-paced or dormant), you can hide the current course instance button.

In data/instances.yml, locate the current course instance and change:

show_in_hero: true
to:
show_in_hero: false
The current course instance can remain in instances.yml; it will simply no longer be displayed as a button in the hero.


4.4.4 Hide the registration button
If the registration for your training is closed, or if the training doesn’t require registration, you can hide the registration button.

In data/instances.yml, change:

registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
to:
registration_url: ""
An empty registration_url tells the template not to display the registration button.


4.4.5 Change action button text
You can also change the text displayed inside either action button without changing where the button links.

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file ui.yml.
Locate:

hero_view_current_label: Take me to the current course instance
hero_registration_open_label: Register now

Replace the text after the colon with the text you want to display.

For example:
hero_view_current_label: View the latest course
hero_registration_open_label: Register for the course
Do not change the names hero_view_current_label or hero_registration_open_label. Only change the text after the colon.

Quick reference
 Configure the hero action buttons 








To…
File
Edit

data/instances.yml
Update slug, label, instance_url, and sort_key to match the current course instance.


Change the registration link
data/instances.yml
Replace the value of registration_url with the URL of your registration page.


Hide the current course button
data/instances.yml
Change show_in_hero: true to show_in_hero: false.


Hide the registration button

title: 4  Landing page
text:
4.5 Course information cards: edit text
The information cards below the hero banner provide key information about your course, including the course content, learning outcomes, topics covered, keywords, course founders, and contributors. Each card can be edited independently.

4.5.1 Change the course content card

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file top-cards.qmd.
Find the Course content card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
Description of the content of the course

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit...
replace the example text with a description of your course.






Tip



Keep the course description concise and focus on what the course covers. Around 10 sentences is usually enough.




4.5.2 Change the learning outcomes card

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file top-cards.qmd.
Find the Learning outcomes card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
1. Learning outcome 1
2. Learning outcome 2
3. Learning outcome 3
replace the example learning outcomes with the learning outcomes for your course.






Tip



Learning outcomes should describe what participants will be able to do after completing the course.
For guidance on writing learning outcomes, see the SciLifeLab Training Hub resource on writing learning outcomes.




4.5.3 Change the keywords card

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file top-cards.qmd.
Find the Keywords card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
- Keyword 1
- Keyword 2
replace the example keywords with keywords that describe your course.






Tip



Around four or five keywords is usually enough. Choose short terms that describe the main subject areas of the course.




4.5.4 Change the topics covered cards

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file top-cards.qmd.
Find the Topics covered card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
- Topic 1
- Topic 2
replace the example topics with the main topics covered by your course.






Tip



Use short phrases rather than complete sentences. Aim to give visitors a quick overview of the main subjects covered by the course.




4.5.5 Change the course founders card
The Course founders card can be used to acknowledge the people who originally developed or established the course.

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file bottom-cards.qmd.
Find the Course founders card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
- Course founder 1
- Course founder 2
replace the example names with the names of the course founders.


4.5.6 Change the course contributors
The Contributors card can be used to acknowledge people who have contributed to the development or maintenance of the course.

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file bottom-cards.qmd.
Find the Contributors card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}

title: 4  Landing page
section: 4.6 Change the course instance banner image
text:
4.6 Change the course instance banner image
The All course instances banner contains a decorative image alongside the links to the available course instances. You can replace this image with an image that represents your course.

4.6.1 1. Add your image

In the main branch, open the img folder and then the images folder.
Add the image you want to use, for example:

my-course-banner.jpg






Tip



A landscape-oriented image works best because the image is cropped automatically to fill the available area.




4.6.2 2. Update the image path

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file instances-band.qmd.
Locate:

  <img src="img/images/navet-band.png" alt="" class="instances-band__image">

Replace img/images/navet-band.png with the path to your image, for example:

<img src="img/images/my-course-banner.jpg" alt="" class="instances-band__image">
The image is decorative, so the alt attribute can remain empty.






Tip



Check how the image appears at different browser widths. The banner automatically crops the image to fill the available space.
If the most important part of your image is being cropped, you can adjust its position in styles.css. Find:
.instances-band__image {
  object-fit: cover;
  object-position: center;
}
Change object-position to move the visible part of the image. For example:
object-position: center top;
or:
object-position: 30% center;

title: 4  Landing page
text:
4.7 Manage course instances
The All course instances banner provides links to the different published instances of your course. This allows visitors to access the current course instance, as well as previous course instances that you choose to make available.
Course instances are managed in data/instances.yml. The instance marked as current is also used for the Take me to the current course instance action button in the hero. Some of the settings described in this section therefore overlap with the instructions for configuring the hero buttons.






Important




Each course instance must have a unique slug. Do not use the same slug for more than one instance!
Only one course instance should be marked as:

status: current

The instance marked as current determines which course instance is treated as the current course throughout the landing page, including the link used by the hero action button. See Mark a course instance as current for instructions.




4.7.1 Add a new course instance

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Copy a full existing course instance entry.
Paste the copied entry under instances:.
Update the slug, label, instance_url and sort key values to describe the new course instance.

For example, for a new course instance taught in November 2026:
- slug: "2611"
  label: "November 2026"
  status: current
  visible: true
  show_in_hero: true
  instance_url: "./2611/"
  registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
  sort_key: 202611


4.7.2 Mark a course instance as current

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Find the previous current instance.
Change:

status: current
to:
status: previous

Set the new current instance to:

status: current
For example:
instances:
  - slug: "2611"
    label: "November 2026"
    status: current
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: true
    instance_url: "./2611/"
    registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
    sort_key: 202611

  - slug: "2605"
    label: "May 2026"
    status: previous
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: false
    instance_url: "./2605/"
    registration_url: ""
    sort_key: 202605


4.7.3 Show or hide a previous instance in the All course instances banner

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
To display an instance in the banner:

visible: true

To hide an instance in the banner:

visible: false
Hiding an instance does not delete it from instances.yml. It simply prevents it from being displayed in the banner.






Important



The instance marked as:
status: current
must always remain:
visible: true
Do not hide the current course instance by setting visible: false. If you do not want the current instance to appear as a button in the hero, use:
show_in_hero: false
instead.




4.7.4 Change the course instance name displayed in the banner

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Change the value for label For example:

label: "May 2026"
can be changed to:
label: "November 2026"
Changing the label only changes the text visitors see. It does not change the course instance URL.


4.7.5 Change the order of course instances
The sort_key determines the chronological order of the course instances.

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Change the value for sort_key. Use the format

YYYYMM
For example:
sort_key: 202605
represents May 2026.

title: 4  Landing page
text:
4.8 Edit the footer
The footer at the bottom of the landing page contains information about the course page development, its licence, and a link to the course repository on GitHub.

4.8.1 Change the footer text

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file footer.qmd.
Locate:

By SciLifeLab Training Hub. Licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

Built with Quarto and hosted on GitHub Pages.

Replace the text with the information you want to display in the footer.







Tip



If you use a licence other than CC BY 4.0, update both the licence name and its link.
In [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/):

replace the text between [ ] with the name of the licence;
replace the URL between ( ) with the corresponding licence URL.





4.8.2 Change the GitHub repository link
The GitHub logo in the footer links visitors to the course repository.

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file footer.qmd.
Locate:

<a href="https://github.com/SciLifeLab-Training/scilifelab-training-template-staging/tree/main" class="landing-footer__image-link">

Replace only the URL inside href="..." with the URL of your course repository.

For example:
<a href="https://github.com/your-organisation/your-course/tree/main" class="landing-footer__image-link">

title: 6  FAIRification and publishing your course
section: 6.2 Make your materials easy to cite
text:
6.2 Make your materials easy to cite
To make your training easier to cite, you can provide citation information in a CITATION.cff file. This file contains structured information about how your training materials should be cited, including the course title, authors, ORCID identifiers, licence, and links to the course repository and website.

6.2.1 Create the citation file for your course
The SciLifeLab Course Page Template already contains a CITATION.cff file in the root of the repository on the main branch. This file describes the template itself. When you use the template for your own course, replace the contents of CITATION.cff with citation information for your own training materials.

In the main branch, open CITATION.cff.
Delete the existing contents of the file.
Copy and paste the following starter text:

cff-version: 1.2.0
message: "If you use these training materials, please cite them as below."

title: "COURSE TITLE"

authors:
  - family-names: "SURNAME"
    given-names: "GIVEN NAME"
    orcid: "https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000"

license: CC-BY-4.0

repository-code: "https://github.com/ORGANISATION/REPOSITORY"
url: "https://ORGANISATION.github.io/REPOSITORY/"

references:
  - type: software
    title: "SciLifeLab Course Page Template"
    repository-code: "PERMANENT TEMPLATE REPOSITORY URL"

Replace the placeholder values with information about your course.








Field
What to enter




title
The title of your course or training materials.


family-names
The author’s family name or surname.


given-names
The author’s given name(s).


orcid
The author’s ORCID identifier, if they have one.


license
The licence under which the training materials are made available.


repository-code
The URL of the GitHub repository containing your course materials.


url
The URL of the published course website.









Important



Keep:
cff-version: 1.2.0
unchanged. This is the version of the Citation File Format specification, not the version of your course.




6.2.2 Add multiple authors
Add a separate entry under authors for each person who should be credited as an author of the training materials.
For example:
authors:
  - family-names: "Smith"
    given-names: "Anna"
    orcid: "https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000"

  - family-names: "Jones"
    given-names: "David"
    orcid: "https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000"
If an author does not have an ORCID, simply omit the orcid line:
authors:
  - family-names: "Jones"
    given-names: "David"






Tip



ORCID provides researchers with a persistent identifier that distinguishes them from other researchers. If your contributors have ORCID identifiers, include them in CITATION.cff.




6.2.3 Acknowledge this template in your course
The starter file contains the following entry:
references:
  - type: software
    title: "SciLifeLab Course Page Template"
    repository-code: "PERMANENT TEMPLATE REPOSITORY URL"
Keep this entry when adapting CITATION.cff for your course. It acknowledges the SciLifeLab Course Page Template as the resource used to create your course website.


6.2.4 Citation files for individual course instances
How you manage CITATION.cff depends on how you publish your course materials.
If your course is maintained as one continuously updated resource, you can maintain the citation information in the main branch.
If individual course instances are released separately (in this template by adding and publishing branches), their citation information may also differ. For example, different instances may have different contributors.
In this case, update CITATION.cff in the specific course-instance branch before creating the release. This allows the citation metadata for that release to reflect the people and materials associated with that particular course instance.






Tip



Before publishing a course instance, check that CITATION.cff contains the correct title, authors, ORCIDs, licence, repository URL, and course website URL for the materials you are releasing.



Quick reference
